<!--
Measured, not read: a table's head cells sit at the foot of their row and
its body cells at the top of theirs, in every format, as the .pdf's booktabs
tables set them and APA's own do. Beside a heading that wraps, a short one
is level with its last line, on the rule; beside a body cell that wraps, a
short one is level with its first.

typst had set every cell at the top, and Word every cell in the middle of
its row.
-->

| Headshort | A heading long enough that it has to wrap onto a second line here, and then words headend | Num |
|:----------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------|----:|
| Bodyshort | Bodystart a body cell long enough that it has to wrap onto a second line inside its column | 12.5 |
| Rowtwo    | 2                                                                    | 3.0  |
